full_reasoning:
Loop 2 of the full-trace arm. Prior context is loop-1's metrics + full_reasoning + execution_algos/vrs-f-l1/NOTES.md (17013 chars, ~4253 tokens). Loop 1 tested using signed mid-drift alignment as a *relaxation* signal -- softening the base vol-skip when sign(drift) matched the order side -- and was decisively refuted: pnl -34.23% vs base, sharpe 1.98 vs 3.07. Loop 1's full_reasoning explicitly identified the symmetric inversion as the most promising next direction: 'aligned trades are *worse* than the base's blind skip, which means adverse-drift trades may be even worse and warrant a tighter skip.'

Hypothesis rationale: I took loop 1's explicit handoff. If the +3,038 aligned-drift trades loop 1 *added* were net-negative-EV (P&L dropped $258 on flat win_rate), by symmetry the adverse-drift subset that the base already partially skips should be *even more* net-negative. So instead of relaxing the skip on aligned-drift trades, tighten it on adverse-drift ones. Concretely: p_eff = max(absolute_floor, p_vol * (1 - adverse_tighten)) when drift opposes order side and |drift| > noise_floor, otherwise pass through unchanged. adverse_tighten=0.5 cuts adverse participation in half; absolute_floor=0.01 (strictly below min_prob=0.05) prevents deterministic null but only binds in the adverse branch.

Design choices vs loop 1: (a) kept the signed-drift EWM (halflife=30, noise_floor=1e-7) and is_aligned helper verbatim -- they are orthogonal plumbing; (b) inverted the aligned branch to a no-op (not a boost) and made the adverse branch the only modification vs base; (c) used a multiplicative tightening rather than additive blending -- this preserves p_eff -> 0 as p_vol -> 0, so the adverse-tightening composes correctly with the base's existing vol-magnitude decay. The reduce-only, cold-start, calm-regime, and SHA-256(client_order_id) draw paths are all unchanged from base/loop 1.

Pre-registered effect-size estimate (in NOTES.md Hypothesis): if symmetry holds, removing ~1,500 adverse trades at ~+$0.085 each should yield ~+$130 / +17% pnl vs base, sharpe improvement larger than pnl improvement. These were loose order-of-magnitude predictions to anchor the test.

Backtest run note: same environment setup as loop 1 -- DATA_CACHE_DIR=/Users/franklinliu/Projects/agentic-trading-system/data-cache (cached locally from prior runs) and S3_BUCKET_NAME=cache-only dummy to satisfy the config. --use-cached-baseline used. All 12 train dates ran.

What the backtest revealed: hypothesis STRONGLY SUPPORTED. vrs-f-l2 cut 3,115 trades vs base (124,876 vs 127,991, -2.43%) -- almost exactly mirroring the +3,038 trades loop 1 added -- and lifted realized_pnl from $753.75 to $980.75 (+30.12%). Sharpe rose from 3.065 to 4.127 (+34.7% relative, +1.063 absolute). Win_rate moved +0.06pp (essentially flat), max_dd improved -0.046% -> -0.042% (~8% smaller). Vs simple baseline, vs_baseline_pnl_pct went from base's +383.17% to +528.69%, and is_weighted_bps improvement deepened from -3.88% to -7.11%.

The implied per-removed-trade contribution is +$227 / 3,115 = ~+$0.073 per skipped trade -- almost exactly symmetric to loop 1's measured -$0.085 per added trade. This is unusually strong consilience: the same direction signal that *added* harm in loop 1 *removed* harm in loop 2, with matching effect size and opposite sign. That symmetry was not pre-guaranteed (the aligned and adverse subsets could have had asymmetric distributions); the data point now makes me much more confident the mid-drift direction is a real adverse-selection axis on this dataset/strategy.

The sharpe improvement outpacing pnl improvement (+34.7% vs +30.1%) is also consistent with removing high-variance, low-edge trades -- exactly the adverse-selection signature: a small subset of trades that contribute disproportionately to variance and drag the mean.

The pre-registered effect-size estimate of +17% pnl was *exceeded* (+30%). This means either (a) the adverse subset's per-trade harm was larger than the aligned subset's per-trade benefit was harmful (asymmetry in our favor), or (b) the loop-1 baseline rate of -$0.085 per added trade was a noisy estimate from a smaller sample. Either way the direction was right; the magnitude was conservative.

What worked: (1) the multiplicative form `p_vol * (1 - adverse_tighten)` composes correctly with the base's vol-decay -- adverse-drift trades in moderately-elevated vol get a small further haircut, while adverse-drift trades in extreme vol get a larger one. (2) Keeping the aligned branch as a no-op preserved the base's behavior in the aligned subset, avoiding loop 1's harm there. (3) absolute_floor=0.01 < min_prob=0.05 ensured the safeguard only binds when the adverse branch fires, not in the base path. (4) Reusing loop 1's drift EWM verbatim made the implementation a one-helper change.

What did not work: nothing in this loop. Both win_rate and drawdown moved in the right direction; no metric regressed.

Implications for future loops in this arm:
- This is the new best algo in the arm. vrs-f-l2 should be the parent for loop 3.
- *Tune `adverse_tighten` upward*: 0.5 was the conservative first cut. With +30% from halving adverse-drift participation, going to 0.7 or 0.9 should test whether the adverse subset is uniformly bad (more tightening helps monotonically) or whether some fraction of adverse-drift trades are actually wins-against-noise (more tightening would start removing wins, capping the gain).
- *Magnitude-conditional tightening*: instead of binary aligned/adverse, use `tighten = sigmoid(-drift_signed / drift_scale)` or similar so larger adverse drifts get tightened more. This is the smooth generalization of the binary cut.
- *Re-tune drift_halflife*: 30 ticks was inherited from loop 1. Try 10 (more reactive) and 60-120 (smoother) to see if the optimal timescale differs from loop 1's choice.
- *Combine with a small aligned boost*: now that we know direction matters, a *very small* aligned-boost (0.05-0.10, not 0.7 like loop 1) might recover some upside without re-introducing significant harm. But this is risky -- loop 1's refutation was decisive and the marginal aligned trades may always be net-negative; safer to leave the aligned branch alone.
- *Different directional signal*: book imbalance, trade aggressor flow, or signed spread state. Each measures something different from mid-drift and may catch a different slice of adverse selection -- could be additive to the mid-drift signal.
- *Parameter tuning of the base vol-skip*: lower min_prob, higher sensitivity to deepen the skip region where the adverse-tightening operates. Risk: amplifies trade-count loss; reward: amplifies the adverse-tightening's effect.
- For the experiment design: this loop confirms that full-trace context matters. The 17,013-char prior context contained the explicit 'try the inversion' handoff from loop 1, which a metrics-only or even brief-summary arm would not have surfaced as cleanly. A useful comparison point against the metrics-only and brief-summary arms of vol-regime-sizer.
